definition.def: Exposure to something dangerous means being in a situation where it might affect you.
examples: Exposure to lead is known to damage the brains of young children. [+ to]
...the potential exposure of people to nuclear waste.

definition.def: Exposure is the harmful effect on your body caused by very cold weather.
examples: He was suffering from exposure and shock but his condition was said to be stable.
At least two people died of exposure in Chicago overnight.

definition.def: The exposure of a well-known person is the revealing of the fact that they are bad or immoral in some way.
examples: ...the exposure of stars in so-called morally compromising situations. [+ of]
Their sporting reputation has suffered enormously from Johnson's exposure.

definition.def: Exposure is publicity that a person, company, or product receives.
examples: The candidates are getting an enormous amount of exposure in the media.

definition.def: In photography, an exposure is a single photograph. [technical]
examples: Larger drawings tend to require two or three exposures to cover them.

definition.def: In photography, the exposure is the amount of light that is allowed to enter a camera when taking a photograph. [technical]
examples: A tripod also lets you shoot long exposures at night.
Against a deep blue sky or dark storm-clouds, you may need to reduce the exposure.
